title: Euler differences evaluated along an integral-ideal filtration on a proper curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a scheme proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], $\mathcal N$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Suppose a finite filtration $0=\mathcal F_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal F_s=\mathcal F$ by coherent submodules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is given, together with quotient isomorphisms $\mathcal Q_a=\mathcal F_a/\mathcal F_{a-1}\cong(h_a)_*\mathcal I_a$, where $h_a:Z_a\hookrightarrow X$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], $Z_a$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and proper over $k$ of dimension zero or one, and $\mathcal I_a\subseteq\mathcal O_{Z_a}$ is a nonzero coherent ideal. Quotients mean cokernels, and pullback and pushforward are those of modules [def-pc-module-pullback]. Write $\mathcal L_a=h_a^*\mathcal N$, use the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and use coherent Euler characteristics [def-pc-euler-characteristic] and degree $\deg_k\mathcal P=\chi(Y,\mathcal P)-\chi(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ for invertible modules on proper $Y/k$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle].

The modules $\mathcal N$, $\mathcal N\otimes\mathcal F_a$, $\mathcal N\otimes\mathcal Q_a$, and $\mathcal L_a\otimes\mathcal I_a$ are coherent, every $\mathcal L_a$ is invertible, and all cohomology groups occurring below are finite-dimensional over $k$ and vanish in sufficiently large degrees. The canonical projection morphism
$$\mathcal N\otimes(h_a)_*\mathcal I_a\longrightarrow(h_a)_*(\mathcal L_a\otimes\mathcal I_a)$$
is an isomorphism. For $\mathcal G_a=\mathcal I_a$ and for $\mathcal G_a=\mathcal L_a\otimes\mathcal I_a$, the canonical closed-pushforward comparisons $H^q(X,(h_a)_*\mathcal G_a)\cong H^q(Z_a,\mathcal G_a)$ are $k$-linear, natural in module morphisms, and compare cohomology computed in structure-sheaf modules on both sides. Put $D(\mathcal G)=\chi(X,\mathcal N\otimes\mathcal G)-\chi(X,\mathcal G)$ for coherent $\mathcal G$ on $X$. Then
$$D(\mathcal F)=\sum_{a=1}^sD(\mathcal Q_a),\qquad D(\mathcal Q_a)=\chi(Z_a,\mathcal L_a\otimes\mathcal I_a)-\chi(Z_a,\mathcal I_a).$$
For a dimension-one $Z_a$, the ideal has generic stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] $\mathcal O_{Z_a,\eta_a}=\kappa(\eta_a)$, where $\kappa(\eta_a)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field], hence generic rank one (the stalk has dimension one over this field), and $D(\mathcal Q_a)=\deg_k(\mathcal L_a)$. For a dimension-zero $Z_a$, its space is one point, $\mathcal L_a$ is globally trivial, and $D(\mathcal Q_a)=0$. In particular
$$\chi(X,\mathcal N\otimes\mathcal F)-\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\sum_{a\in\{1,\ldots,s\},\,\dim Z_a=1}\deg_k(h_a^*\mathcal N).$$
The identities include $s=0$ and $\mathcal F=0$, with zero Euler differences and empty sums.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent] to $X$ and to each $Z_a$: all these schemes are Noetherian, and $\mathcal N$ is coherent. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-invertible], $\mathcal L_a=h_a^*\mathcal N$ is invertible. The coherent-kernel/cokernel assertion [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth], applied to $\mathcal F_{a-1}\to\mathcal F_a$, makes $\mathcal Q_a$ coherent. These applications use properness over the given field, not smoothness or geometric integrality.

For an invertible module $\mathcal P$ and any module $\mathcal H$, choose open neighbourhoods trivializing $\mathcal P$ as in [def-sc-invertible-module]. On each such open, $\mathcal P\otimes\mathcal H$ is $\mathcal H$, and a sequence tensored with $\mathcal P$ identifies with the original sequence, including its maps. Thus tensoring preserves short exact sequences. If $\mathcal H$ is coherent, the local finite-generation and kernel conditions of [pqf-def-coherent] also hold for $\mathcal P\otimes\mathcal H$, hence it is coherent. Apply this to $(\mathcal N,\mathcal F_a)$, $(\mathcal N,\mathcal Q_a)$ and $(\mathcal L_a,\mathcal I_a)$. In particular both $0\to\mathcal F_{a-1}\to\mathcal F_a\to\mathcal Q_a\to0$ and its $\mathcal N$-tensor are short exact coherent sequences.

source.place: Tag 0AYW (lemma-degree-in-terms-of-components), proof: tensoring the coherent short exact sequence with a locally free module; local rank-one verification.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined] on $X$ to $\mathcal F_a$, $\mathcal Q_a$, $\mathcal N$, and their twists, and on each $Z_a$ to $\mathcal I_a$, $\mathcal L_a\otimes\mathcal I_a$, $\mathcal L_a$ and $\mathcal O_{Z_a}$. These modules are coherent by the hypotheses and steps 1--2. Each cohomology group in the asserted formulas is consequently finite-dimensional over $k$, with only finitely many nonzero degrees. Closed pushforwards appearing in comparisons are coherent by [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology], so the same conclusion applies to them.

Use the projection clause of [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] for $h_a$, $\mathcal I_a$ and $\mathcal N$. Composing with tensor symmetry on its source and target gives the stated map $\mathcal N\otimes(h_a)_*\mathcal I_a\to(h_a)_*(\mathcal L_a\otimes\mathcal I_a)$, an isomorphism. Explicitly, on a trivializing open for $\mathcal N$, the section map sends $n\otimes m$ to $h_a^*n\otimes m$ and identifies with the identity on $(h_a)_*\mathcal I_a$. This also identifies it with the canonical projection morphism, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism. The locally Noetherian hypotheses hold by step 1.

source.place: Tag 01E8 (lemma-projection-formula), locally free rank-one case; local trivialization as in the existing closed-immersion node.

proof.text: For any coherent $\mathcal G$ on $Z_a$, compose the canonical module-to-abelian comparison on $X$, the natural closed-embedding abelian comparison, and the inverse module-to-abelian comparison on $Z_a$. These are supplied by [lem-sc-zariski-module-abelian-cohomology-agree] and [lem-sc-cohomology-closed-immersion-pushforward]. The abelian sheaf underlying $(h_a)_*\mathcal G$ has sections $\mathcal G(h_a^{-1}U)$, exactly the abelian direct image. Thus the composite compares structure-sheaf-module cohomology on both sides and is natural in every module morphism. For $c\in k$, multiplication by its structure-section is a module endomorphism of $\mathcal G$, and its pushforward is multiplication by $c$ on $(h_a)_*\mathcal G$, since $h_a$ is over $k$. Naturality gives $e_q(c v)=c e_q(v)$; additivity gives $k$-linearity. Take $\mathcal G=\mathcal I_a$ and $\mathcal G=\mathcal L_a\otimes\mathcal I_a$.

Apply [lem-pc-euler-additive] to each of the two short exact sequences of step 2 and subtract: $D(\mathcal F_a)=D(\mathcal F_{a-1})+D(\mathcal Q_a)$. The base is $D(\mathcal F_0)=D(0)=0$: tensor sends the zero module to zero, and all its cohomology vector spaces are zero. Induction gives $D(\mathcal F_b)=\sum_{a=1}^bD(\mathcal Q_a)$ for $0\le b\le s$, hence the first asserted equality. Furthermore the given quotient isomorphism, the projection isomorphism of step 4, and the $k$-linear cohomology isomorphisms of step 5 identify the two finite alternating dimension sums. Therefore $D(\mathcal Q_a)=\chi(Z_a,\mathcal L_a\otimes\mathcal I_a)-\chi(Z_a,\mathcal I_a)$.

source.place: Tag 08AA (lemma-euler-characteristic-additive), applied successively; Tag 0AYW (lemma-degree-in-terms-of-components), Euler subtraction in its proof.

proof.text: If $\dim Z_a=1$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-scheme-ideal-generic-stalk] to the nonzero ideal $\mathcal I_a$. It is quasi-coherent because it is coherent on the locally Noetherian $Z_a$, by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. The result gives $(\mathcal I_a)_{\eta_a}=\mathcal O_{Z_a,\eta_a}$, a field, hence the residue field $\kappa(\eta_a)$, with dimension one over itself. Apply [lem-trf-curve-euler-tensor-generic-rank] with $C=Z_a$, $\mathcal L=\mathcal L_a$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal I_a$, and $r=1$. Subtracting $\chi(Z_a,\mathcal I_a)$ in that formula and using step 6 yields $D(\mathcal Q_a)=\deg_k(\mathcal L_a)$. All hypotheses are present: $Z_a$ is integral, proper and one-dimensional, $\mathcal I_a$ coherent, and $\mathcal L_a$ invertible.

source.place: Tag 0AYV (lemma-degree-on-proper-curve), rank-one specialization; coherent.tex Tag 01YL, nonzero integral ideals at the generic point.

proof.text: If $\dim Z_a=0$, [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-finite-discrete] applies by step 1 and makes $|Z_a|$ finite discrete. Integrality [def-pc-integral-scheme] makes it nonempty and irreducible. A discrete irreducible nonempty space has one point: if there were two, one singleton and its complement would be disjoint nonempty opens. A trivializing neighbourhood of that point for the invertible $\mathcal L_a$ is consequently all of $Z_a$, so $\mathcal L_a\cong\mathcal O_{Z_a}$ by [def-sc-invertible-module]. Tensoring this isomorphism with $\mathcal I_a$ gives $\mathcal L_a\otimes\mathcal I_a\cong\mathcal I_a$, and their Euler characteristics agree. Step 6 therefore gives $D(\mathcal Q_a)=0$. Substituting this and step 7 into the finite filtration sum leaves exactly the sum over dimension-one factors asserted in the statement. For $s=0$, the filtration forces $\mathcal F=0$ and the base case in step 6 is the empty-sum identity; if $\mathcal F=0$ no nonzero ideal factors can occur, since the given quotient isomorphisms would otherwise identify a zero module with a nonzero closed pushforward.

source.place: Tag 0AAX (lemma-locally-Noetherian-dimension-0); varieties.tex Tag 0AYT (lemma-chi-tensor-finite), rank-one zero-dimensional case.

from.place: The fibrewise ampleness-to-projectivity argument: positivity on normalized geometric-fibre components is converted to relative ampleness and then to a projective-bundle embedding. Supporting input: the proper integral curve degree criterion (0B5X). In the 0B5X proof this is the tensor-product degree formula used to pass from the degree of a positive tensor power to the degree of the line bundle and to obtain linear Euler-characteristic growth. Supporting input: the multiplicity-weighted reduction to reduced integral components in the proof of Stacks 0AYX (via 0AYW). Extraction: Original item proof step 1 (invertible and tensor coherence, finite Euler sums) and steps 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10: exact tensor devissage, local projection isomorphism, k-linear closed-pushforward cohomology, and evaluation on one- and zero-dimensional integral ideals.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q96-a66fb0314 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 8 steps in full. The delivery creates no new nodes and leaves the statement and stmt_deps unchanged; the item had no proof before. It carries no repair note and its proof closure has no cycle. Source: Stacks varieties.tex 0AYW and 0AYV, with tag labels checked against tags/tags. The item is a correct agent-written generalisation of the 0AYW induction. Step 1: proper-field-invertible-coherent on X and on each Z_a, invertible pullback, and coherent cokernel for F_{a-1}->F_a. Step 2 (elementary): an invertible twist is locally the identity, so it is exact and keeps coherence. Step 3: Euler finiteness, and closed pushforwards are coherent. Step 4: the projection clause of lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology. Step 5: 03FD composed with 02UV. def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology is H(X_Zar), so the two notions match; naturality applied to multiplication by c gives k-linearity. Step 6: the first formula of 08AA plus induction on the filtration, then evaluation on Z_a. Step 7: a nonzero ideal has generic stalk equal to the field, so r=1 in lem-trf-curve-euler-tensor-generic-rank, which needs no smoothness. Step 8: zero-dimensional Noetherian implies finite discrete, and integral then gives a single point, so the line bundle is trivial and D=0. Edge cases s=0 and F=0 checked. The DAG has no duplicate of the item. All 10 tool_uses are generic tools, and I accept them. Advisory: the k-structure on Z_a is implicitly the one through X.
